slides.title: Is this [[you]]?
items: You keep peeling off dry bits
Corners of your lips feel tight

slides.title: Lips have [[little oil]]
slides.body: Lip skin is thinner than the rest of your face and has almost no oil glands. So when cold, dry air arrives, your lips feel it first.

slides.title: The [[licking]] habit
slides.body: Licking feels nice for a second, but as saliva dries it takes moisture with it. The more you lick, the drier your lips can feel.

items.head: Don't peel the flakes
items.sub: Soften them after a warm shower

items.head: Reapply balm often
items.sub: After meals and right before bed

items.head: Sip water, don't lick
items.sub: Reach for water when lips feel dry

slides.title: Lip care [[checklist]]
slides.note: Lifestyle tips only. If it lasts, talk to a professional.

slides.title: Keep shining with [[Glow]]!
slides.body: Save, share and tell a friend

caption:
Cold air, flaky lips? 💋

Lips have almost no oil glands, so dry air reaches them first, and licking takes away what little moisture is left.
Try three small habits starting tonight:
Don't peel the flakes · Reapply balm often · Sip water instead of licking
